title: Delhi Wakes to Post-Diwali Smog as AQI Hits 368, 15 Areas Turn Severe
excerpt: A day after Diwali, every one of Delhi's 54 monitoring stations read above 200, 15 crossed into the severe band, and PM2.5 near Akshardham peaked at more than 50 times the WHO daily limit late on Sunday night.
body:
• Delhi's overall AQI was 368 at 7 a.m. on Monday, in the 'very poor' category, with PM2.5 as the major pollutant, according to Central Pollution Control Board data reported by Data Street.
  • All 54 monitoring stations read above 200, 50 read above 300, and 15 areas were 'severe' above 400; Burari Crossing and Sonia Vihar topped the 7 a.m. list at 441 each.
  • PM2.5 near Akshardham reached 760.99 micrograms per cubic metre at 11 p.m. on Sunday — more than 50 times the WHO's recommended 24-hour limit of 15.
  • For readers in Delhi: Stage III GRAP curbs remain in force, and the Air Quality Early Warning System forecast severe air for the next few days — limit outdoor exertion, especially for children and people with respiratory disease.

New Delhi woke on Monday to a thick layer of smog a day after Diwali, with the city's overall Air Quality Index at 368 at 7 a.m., in the 'very poor' category, according to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data. A dense blanket of smog covered several parts of the capital in the morning hours and considerably reduced visibility, IANS reported.

Severe air in 15 areas

The deterioration was citywide rather than localised. Data from 54 monitoring stations showed every station above 200, 50 stations above 300, and 15 areas in the 'severe' band above 400. Burari Crossing and Sonia Vihar recorded 441 each at 7 a.m., followed by Vivek Vihar at 437, Delhi Technological University at 434, Delhi University's North Campus and Jahangirpuri at 433, Rohini at 430 and Bawana at 424. The CPCB classifies AQI between 301 and 400 as 'very poor' and 401 to 500 as 'severe'. Delhi's daily average AQI settled at 376 on Sunday, up from 369 a day earlier, according to the CPCB figures reported by The Hindu BusinessLine and IANS.

The sharpest spike came late on Diwali night. The Delhi Pollution Control Committee noted that PM2.5 near Akshardham soared to 760.99 micrograms per cubic metre at 11 p.m. on Sunday, more than 50 times the World Health Organization's recommended 24-hour exposure limit of 15 micrograms per cubic metre — an hourly peak, not a daily average, but a measure of the intensity of the spike.

Crackers beyond the permitted windows

The Supreme Court had allowed certified green crackers in Delhi-NCR only in two windows on November 7 and 8 — 6 a.m. to 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. Reports from several neighbourhoods said firecrackers continued well beyond the 10 p.m. deadline, and conventional firecrackers were also used in parts of the city. IANS reported separately that the Delhi Pollution Control Committee's website stopped displaying live readings from several monitoring stations for a few hours on Diwali night, including stations at R.K. Puram, Nehru Nagar, Mundka, Sonia Vihar and Dwarka, raising questions about data availability at the peak.

Curbs in force, severe air forecast

Delhi-NCR remains under Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan, activated by the Commission for Air Quality Management on November 6, which bans non-essential construction and demolition, restricts certain diesel vehicles and tightens industrial controls. Additional winter measures in force since November 1 include restrictions on non-BS-VI vehicles registered outside Delhi and a 'No PUC, No Fuel' policy. The Air Quality Early Warning System forecast that Delhi's air would remain in the 'severe' category from November 9 for the next few days, with vehicular emissions and peak stubble-burning season adding to firecracker emissions, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. Across the wider NCR at 7 a.m., Ghaziabad read 366, Bahadurgarh 389, Noida 340, Faridabad 334 and Gurugram 316.

nri_angle: For NRIs with family in Delhi, Monday's readings are the practical test of the visit-and-health advice issued before Diwali: the air stayed in the very poor to severe band across the whole city, not just in hotspots.
